title: SURF: Steering the Scalarization Weight to Uniformly Traverse the Pareto Front
claim: Steering the scalarization weight by the path's geometry gives evenly spaced solutions along the trade-off front, while uniform weights bunch them unevenly.
layout: single panel, 2-D front with rainbow weight colorbar at right, gear inset
description: A single 2-D plot with axes h1 and h2 shows a convex dashed black Pareto front curving from the top-left down to the bottom-right. Blue asterisks, labeled with uniform weights 0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8 and 1, mark where uniform weight sampling lands. They are unevenly spaced along the curve. Rainbow-colored circles sit at evenly spaced positions on the front, with matching colored arrows pointing along it. A vertical rainbow colorbar on the right maps those circles to non-uniform weights: 0.0, 0.26, 0.52, 0.68, 0.76 and 1.0. In the upper right, the title 'Gearing weight w to SURF uniformly' has SURF in rainbow letters. Below it, a gear labeled Φ(w) with a rainbow circular arrow suggests the weight is being remapped. The eye goes first to the colorful title and gear, then to the curve.
caption: Multi-armed bandit LS results (details in Appendix [ref]). Uniform weights produce uneven points on PF (stars), while PF-aware sampling yields uniformly spaced colored circles.
abstract: Scalarization is widely used in multi-objective optimization owing to its simplicity and scalability. In many applications, the goal is to generate solutions that represent diverse user preferences, ideally with uniform coverage of the Pareto front (PF). However, uniformly sampling scalarization weights usually induces non-uniform coverage of the PF. We explain this mismatch through the geometry of the scalarization path. As the weight varies, the corresponding solutions traverse the PF at a generally nonuniform speed. Integrating this speed gives cumulative arc length. After normalization by the total length, it defines a cumulative distribution function (CDF) on weights whose inverse selects points at equal arc-length intervals. Building on this insight, we propose SURF (Sampling Uniformly along the Pareto Front). For structured problems, including bi-objective bandits, we derive analytical expressions for this CDF map and the resulting PF-aware weight sampling rule. For general problems, SURF alternates between CDF reconstruction and weight sampling. Theoretically, we show that under provable conditions for bi-objective LS, SURF's CDF reconstruction error converges linearly to an $O(N^{-2})$ discretization floor. Empirically, experiments on bandits, multi-objective-gymnasium, and multi-objective LLM alignment demonstrate that SURF efficiently achieves more uniform PF coverage than baselines.
